answer.rationale: p99 latency climbing 5x over 90 minutes during settlement peak with heavy writes indicates capacity constraint under load, not code regression. The security patch cannot be reverted per compliance. Rollback is ruled out. Read replica routing (memory_b5) addresses read load but settlement traffic is write-heavy, so limited benefit. Circuit breaker (memory_b4) would degrade service. Regional failover (memory_b2) is a fallback if capacity addition fails, but adds complexity during peak writes. Adding capacity directly addresses the bottleneck: memory_b3 shows provisioning headroom successfully absorbed surge traffic; memory_b5 demonstrates successful load shedding via replica routing works but won't solve write-path saturation. Capacity addition is the highest-confidence intervention that preserves the mandatory security patch, avoids write loss during peak settlement, and can execute within one intervention window.
